docs.title: Accordion Agenda Guide
docs.text:
Version 1.1.003 — Review Edition

This shared guide is for Group Administrators and District Administrators who prepare, review, publish, and revise Accordion Agendas.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Who should use this guide: An authorized Group or District Administrator responsible for meeting agendas.

Required access: Group Administrator access to the Board or committee group that owns the agenda.

Recommended starting point: Use an approved reusable template and work in Draft Mode until review is complete.

docs.title: Recommended workflow
docs.text:
1. Open Drafts & Templates.
  2. Clone the approved template for the meeting type.
  3. Update the title, date, time, header, and placeholder content.
  4. Actively select the correct Group.
  5. Work in Draft Mode: Private, Notifications unchecked, Published unchecked.
  6. Save frequently and review the saved agenda.
  7. Build or update sections, agenda items, expandable HTML, and attachments.
  8. Verify public and private content.
  9. Publish, send the intended notifications, and verify the signed-out public view.

Figure SB-AAC-001. Clone an approved template whenever possible.

Preferred method

Clone the appropriate meeting template. Use Add Content to build from scratch only when no suitable template exists.

Ask before guessing

Stop and ask whenever Group assignment, visibility, publication, notifications, or confidential attachments are unclear. There are no stupid questions.

docs.title: Anatomy of an Accordion Agenda
docs.text:
An Accordion Agenda is built from nested components. Understanding their relationship makes editing and troubleshooting much easier.

Figure SB-AAC-014. Anatomy of a completed Accordion Agenda section.

docs.title: Accordion Section
docs.text:
An Accordion Section is an agenda heading, such as Finance, Superintendent, Public Comment, or Executive Session. Build the agenda one section at a time.

Figure SB-AAC-015. A saved Accordion Section.

docs.title: Agenda Item
docs.text: An Agenda Item belongs inside an Accordion Section. Use it for the actual matter under consideration, such as a report, discussion item, motion, resolution, presentation, or approval.

docs.title: Expandable HTML
docs.text:
Expandable HTML provides an accessible on-page alternative to relying only on a PDF.

  • Read text becomes the button or link label.
  • HTML contains the accessible document content.
  • Public expandable HTML is available to every visitor.
  • Private expandable HTML is visible only to authorized group members.

Use a descriptive label such as Read Superintendent's Report. For confidential content, use a clearly marked label such as Private: Read Executive Session Materials.

docs.title: Public and private files
docs.text:
• Public files are visible to everyone after publication.
  • Private files are visible only to authorized, signed-in group members.

Verify confidential material

Before publication, confirm that every confidential file and expandable item is beneath the correct private heading. Preview is an administrator view and cannot prove what an anonymous visitor will see.

docs.title: Component hierarchy
docs.text:
Accordion Agenda
└── Accordion Section
    └── Agenda Item
        ├── Public Expandable HTML
        ├── Public File
        ├── Private Expandable HTML
        └── Private File

docs.title: Conventions Used in This Guide
docs.text:
Tip or Best Practice

A recommended method that saves time, improves consistency, or reduces avoidable errors.

Note

Helpful background information or a related detail.

Important

A step that deserves particular attention because overlooking it may cause an agenda, access, or notification problem.

Warning

A privacy, publication, notification, or security risk. Stop and verify the setting before continuing.

docs.title: Preferred and alternative methods
docs.text: The preferred method is schoolboard.net's normal recommended workflow. An alternative method may be appropriate when the preferred method does not fit the meeting.

docs.title: Phones and tablets
docs.text:
1. Select ☰ Topics to open the guide navigation.
  2. Select a page.
  3. Select the page-outline icon to open the page Table of Contents.
  4. Select a heading to move directly to that section.

The current page title remains above the Table of Contents so its context is not lost while scrolling.

docs.title: Work Safely in Draft Mode
docs.text: An agenda remains a draft until Published is selected. schoolboard.net recommends saving and reviewing the agenda in Draft Mode rather than keeping unsaved work in Preview.

docs.title: Draft Mode settings
docs.text:
• Visibility: Private
  • Notifications: Unchecked
  • Published: Unchecked

These settings allow the agenda to be saved repeatedly without making it public or sending notifications.

docs.title: Recommended review process
docs.text:
1. Clone a template or begin a new agenda.
  2. Confirm the three Draft Mode settings.
  3. Save frequently while editing.
  4. Open and review the saved draft.
  5. Ask another authorized administrator to review it when district procedure requires a second review.
  6. Revise and save again as needed.
  7. Publish only after the agenda and all attachments are approved.

docs.title: Why Draft Mode is safer than Preview
docs.text:
• Work is preserved after every save.
  • You may leave and return later.
  • Another authorized administrator can review the saved draft.
  • Review uses the actual saved content rather than an unsaved in-memory preview.
  • The agenda remains unavailable to the public.
  • No notification is sent accidentally.

Preview is an administrator view

Preview does not simulate the anonymous public view. After publication, sign out and open the agenda as a public visitor.

Check all three settings

Private visibility alone does not define Draft Mode. Confirm that Notifications and Published are also unchecked.

docs.title: Templates and Cloning
docs.text: Most districts maintain a separate master template for each recurring meeting type. Templates preserve the district's approved structure and dramatically reduce preparation time.

docs.title: Common templates
docs.text:
• Regular Board Meeting
  • Regular Board Meeting with Closed Session
  • Work Session
  • Special Meeting
  • Budget Workshop
  • Organizational Meeting
  • Committee Meeting

Figure SB-AAC-002. A reusable master template may contain recurring sections, agenda items, and expandable HTML.

docs.title: Find the correct template
docs.text:
Open Drafts & Templates from the group home page. The list sorts by meeting date in reverse order, newest first.

  • Current drafts appear near the top.
  • Give permanent templates an intentionally older date so they remain near the bottom.
  • Select Show More when a template is not immediately visible.

Figure SB-AAC-010. Select Show More to display older templates.

docs.title: Clone the template
docs.text:
1. Open the approved template for the meeting type.
  2. Select Clone from the top menu.

Figure SB-AAC-008. Select Clone from the template's top menu.

  1. Replace the Clone of... title with the correct meeting title.
  2. Update the date, time, agenda header, and placeholder text.
  3. Click the correct Group, even if it already appears highlighted.
  4. Confirm Draft Mode settings.
  5. Save. The independent agenda appears in Drafts & Templates.

Figure SB-AAC-009. Update the clone and actively select its Group.

A highlighted Group may not be selected

Always click the destination Group before saving. An unassigned agenda can appear to be missing, fail to display on the expected group page, and notify the wrong audience or no audience.

docs.title: Protect master templates
docs.text:
• Limit structural template changes to designated administrators.
  • Never convert the master template into a current meeting agenda.
  • Change a template only when the district intentionally changes its standard format.
  • Maintain distinct templates for meeting types with different structures.
  • Add reusable blank expandable HTML blocks when they reduce repetitive work.

Need a new template?

Send schoolboard.net Support an approved outline, Word document, or sample agenda. The “magical elves” can build a reusable template, often providing the quickest way to learn the system and establish a consistent starting point.
